title: Norwalk state hospital police chief, officer charged in alleged timecard fraud sheme - NewsBreak
text:
By No media credit provided. ,
9 hours ago
The police chief and an officer at a California state psychiatric hospital in Norwalk are facing felony grand theft charges in an alleged timecard fraud scheme, officials announced Wednesday.
“We will prove this was a coordinated, deliberate scheme between a police chief and his officer to take taxpayer money for work that was never done,” Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said.
From November 2022 through April 2023, former Chief of Police for the California Department of State Hospitals – Metropolitan in Norwalk, Donald Santarin Salvador, 44, and former hospital police officer Daniel James Beauregard, 52, allegedly schemed to submit timecards for hours that Beauregard did not spend performing police duties, according to the District Attorney’s Office.
Prosecutors say that instead of working for the hospital, Beauregard worked on projects for a private business owned by Salvador. The business was identified as a security consulting company, Daly Strategic Group LLC.
“This former police chief and officer clocked in for work, little did we know they would allegedly be working for their own private business and not the people of California,” Hochman said. “They collected government paychecks while conducting their own side hustle. That’s not public service, it’s the betrayal of the public’s trust, and we will hold them accountable in court.”
Salvador, of Lake Forest, and Beauregard, of Northridge, were each charged with one count of grand theft.
The District Attorney’s Office said the estimated losses exceeded $40,000. If convicted as charged, Salvador and Beauregard each face up to three years in state prison, to be served in county jail.
Department of State Hospitals, Metropolitan primarily treats adults with serious mental health disorders who are placed there through the legal system. Due to community concerns, the facility does not accept patients with criminal histories that include murder, sex crimes, or escape, according to the hospital’s website .
